mechanism: Propylthiouracil can cause agranulocytosis and immunosuppression, while bumetanide may cause hypokalemia and metabolic alkalosis, both increasing infection risk and electrolyte complications in hyperthyroid patients.
action: Monitor electrolytes (particularly potassium), complete blood counts, and infection signs; ensure adequate potassium supplementation if needed; consider alternative diuretics with less electrolyte depletion if possible.
